source_text: Tunica linea ad cutem — castitas interior. Homo communis peccatis servus; sacerdos novus induitur Christo.
thought_title: The linen tunic and the new priest
orientation: Origen is interpreting the high priest's garments spiritually, applying each item to the moral life of the believer.
pass_a_gloss: The linen tunic against the skin — interior chastity. The common man is a slave to sins; the new priest is clothed with Christ.

choices.english: The linen tunic against the skin
choices.why: Keeps the physical contact of the garment with the body, which is the point of the spiritual reading.
rejected: The linen tunic next to the skin

choices.why: Preserves the noun-adjective order and the moral sense of purity of soul.
Renders communis as ordinary or unregenerate, contrasting with the new priest.
Keeps the dative of servitude and the plural peccatis as the master.
Preserves the adjective novus, which signals the regenerate state in Christ.
Uses the passive with ablative to match the Latin construction and the baptismal imagery.

pass_b_english: The linen tunic worn against the skin is interior chastity. The common man is a slave to sins; the new priest is clothed with Christ.
